title: India Strengthens Regional Health Partnerships as First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting Unanimously Adopts Joint Ministerial Statement in Colombo
subtitle:
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Leads India’s Engagement at Historic Meeting; BIMSTEC Countries Adopt Revised Plan of Action on Public Health (2026–2030)
India and Sri Lanka Deepen Healthcare Partnership; MoU Exchanged for 100 Additional Ambulances under Indian Grant Assistance of Approximately USD 5.28 Million
Shri Nadda Announces Indian Support for 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs to Strengthen Primary Healthcare Services in Sri Lanka
India to Host BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at ITRA, Jamnagar, Gujarat
Union Health Minister Holds Bilateral Meetings with Health Ministers of Sri Lanka and Nepal to Strengthen Healthcare Cooperation
Shri Nadda Highlights India’s Healthcare Transformation and Offers to Share Expertise in Primary Healthcare, Digital Health and Public Health Infrastructure with BIMSTEC Countries
Union Health Minister Interacts with Indian Diaspora in Colombo; Highlights India’s Growing Global Leadership and Strong India–Sri Lanka Partnership
“No Country Should Be Left Behind in Its Pursuit of Better Health Outcomes”: Shri J.P. Nadda
body_text: In a major step towards strengthening regional health cooperation, the First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting held in Colombo, Sri Lanka, today unanimously adopted a Joint Ministerial Statement, reaffirming the collective commitment of member countries to advancing accessible, affordable and quality healthcare, strengthening regional health security and building resilient public health systems across the Bay of Bengal region. Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, represented India at the historic meeting, highlighting the country's growing role in advancing regional health cooperation through knowledge-sharing, digital innovation, capacity building and collaborative action on common public health challenges. The meeting also adopted the Revised BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Public Health (2026–2030), providing a structured roadmap for cooperation in disease surveillance, pandemic preparedness, digital health, traditional medicine, One Health and healthcare workforce development. India's engagement at the meeting was further marked by significant bilateral initiatives with Sri Lanka, including the exchange of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the supply of 100 additional fully-equipped ambulances and the announcement of support for 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs to strengthen primary healthcare services. Shri Nadda also held bilateral discussions with Nepal's Health Minister and interacted with the Indian diaspora in Colombo, reaffirming India's commitment to strengthening its longstanding partnerships in the region. BIMSTEC Health Ministers Unanimously Adopt Joint Ministerial Statement Addressing the inaugural meeting, Shri Nadda described the occasion as a landmark in regional cooperation, following the decision taken at the Sixth BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok in April 2025 to establish a dedicated mechanism for cooperation among Health Ministers of member countries. He emphasised that BIMSTEC countries share both a collective responsibility and a significant opportunity to strengthen healthcare systems, improve access to quality health services and enhance preparedness against emerging health challenges. The unanimously adopted Joint Ministerial Statement underscores the commitment of member countries to Universal Health Coverage and Sustainable Development Goal 3, while identifying key priorities for coordinated regional action. The Statement provides a forward-looking framework for strengthening disease surveillance, emergency preparedness, early warning systems, antimicrobial resistance management, digital healthcare, traditional medicine, climate-related health responses and capacity building. It also envisages exploring a BIMSTEC Digital Health Framework to promote telemedicine, interoperable electronic health records and the use of Artificial Intelligence in diagnostics and disease modelling. The meeting welcomed regional initiatives, including the proposed BIMSTEC Regional Centre of Excellence for Public Health in Sri Lanka, the establishment of the BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence on Tropical Medicine in Thailand, and India's initiative to establish a Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine. The Joint Ministerial Statement also welcomed Bangladesh's proposal for a Regional Zoonotic Disease Observatory and Early Warning System and underscored the importance of strengthening coordinated preparedness against cross-border health threats. India Offers to Share Its Healthcare Expertise with BIMSTEC Countries Highlighting India's progress towards Universal Health Coverage under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Nadda outlined the country's comprehensive approach to healthcare, combining expanded primary healthcare services, financial protection, modern public health infrastructure and digital innovation. He informed the gathering that India has established over 1.85 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs , bringing comprehensive primary healthcare services closer to communities and improving access to preventive, promotive and essential healthcare. The Minister also highlighted Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), one of the world's largest publicly funded health assurance schemes, providing annual cashless hospitalisation coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per eligible family and covering over 60 crore people. Referring to the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM), he underscored India's investments in strengthening public health infrastructure, disease surveillance, diagnostic capabilities and preparedness for future health emergencies. Shri Nadda also highlighted the transformative role of technology in expanding healthcare access, noting that India's National Telemedicine Service, eSanjeevani, has crossed 50 crore teleconsultations . He outlined India's experience under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) in building an interoperable digital health ecosystem to improve healthcare accessibility, efficiency and continuity of care. Reaffirming India's commitment to regional cooperation, Shri Nadda offered to share the country's experience, technical expertise and best practices with BIMSTEC Member States, particularly in primary healthcare, digital health systems and public health infrastructure. India to Host BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at Jamnagar In a significant initiative to deepen regional cooperation in traditional medicine, Shri Nadda announced India's commitment to hosting the BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, Gujarat . The Centre is envisaged as a regional platform for collaborative research, academic exchanges, institutional partnerships, capacity building and the sharing of traditional medicine knowledge and best practices. It will also promote evidence-informed approaches, quality and safety standards, and the responsible preservation of traditional knowledge. The Joint Ministerial Statement welcomed India's initiative, recognising its potential to strengthen regional cooperation in traditional medicine. India's proposal to host the next meeting of the BIMSTEC Task Force on Traditional Medicine was also welcomed. Underscoring the importance of collective preparedness, Shri Nadda called for greater regional cooperation under the One Health approach. He highlighted that the approach aligns with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of “One Earth, One Family, One Future” , rooted in India's ancient philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam representing India's long-held integrated approach to global health, sustainability and collaborative governance. The Minister emphasised that that One Health is a shared responsibility and early detection, timely information-sharing and coordinated action are essential to preventing disease outbreaks and safeguarding public health. India and Sri Lanka Deepen Healthcare Partnership; MoU Exchanged for 100 Additional Ambulances On the sidelines of the BIMSTEC meeting, Shri J.P. Nadda held a high-level bilateral meeting with Sri Lanka's Minister of Health and Mass Media, Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa, to review ongoing health initiatives and explore opportunities for further strengthening cooperation between the two countries. In a significant outcome of the meeting, the two Ministers witnessed the exchange of an MoU for the supply of 100 additional fully-equipped ambulances to Sri Lanka's 1990 Suwa Seriya Emergency Ambulance Service. The initiative will be supported through Indian grant assistance of SLR 1,725.73 million (approximately USD 5.28 million) and is expected to further strengthen emergency medical response capabilities, improve operational efficiency and facilitate timely access to emergency healthcare services across Sri Lanka. India has been a longstanding development partner in the establishment and expansion of the Suwa Seriya service, having earlier extended grant assistance of USD 7.5 million in 2016 and USD 15.02 million in 2018. These initiatives supported the deployment of 297 ambulances, which have played a vital role in providing emergency medical assistance, including during the COVID-19 pandemic and natural disasters. The additional 100 ambulances will further build upon this successful partnership and strengthen Sri Lanka's emergency healthcare network. India Announces Support for 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs in Sri Lanka Further strengthening bilateral healthcare cooperation, Shri Nadda announced India's support for the procurement of 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs to enhance primary healthcare delivery in Sri Lanka. The initiative, involving Indian grant assistance of up to SLR 225 million , forms part of the USD 450 million comprehensive rehabilitation package announced by the Government of India following Cyclone Ditwah, which affected Sri Lanka during November–December 2025. The Medical Kiosks will be deployed at Sri Lanka's Arogya Primary Health Centres to provide point-of-care diagnostic services integrated with telemedicine facilities. The initiative is expected to improve access to essential diagnostic services, enable timely medical consultations and strengthen technology-enabled primary healthcare delivery, particularly for communities requiring accessible and efficient healthcare services. These initiatives reflect India's continued commitment to supporting Sri Lanka's health system and advancing a development partnership focused on delivering tangible benefits to people. Shri Nadda Meets Nepal's Health Minister; Discusses Stronger Bilateral and Regional Health Cooperation Shri Nadda also held a bilateral meeting with Nepal's Minister for Health and Food Safety, Ms. Neesha Mehta, on the sidelines of the First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting. The two Ministers held fruitful discussions on deepening bilateral and regional health cooperation, sharing expertise and best practices, and improving access to affordable, accessible and quality healthcare. The meeting reaffirmed the deep-rooted historical, cultural and people-to-people ties between India and Nepal, which continue to provide a strong foundation for cooperation in healthcare and development. Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Neighbourhood First policy , India reiterated its commitment to working closely with Nepal to strengthen healthcare partnerships, promote improved health outcomes and advance shared regional prosperity. Union Health Minister Interacts with Indian Diaspora in Colombo During his visit, Shri Nadda also interacted with members of the Indian diaspora in Colombo, acknowledging their invaluable contribution to strengthening the longstanding friendship and people-to-people ties between India and Sri Lanka. Addressing the gathering, the Union Health Minister highlighted India's remarkable progress over the past 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, particularly in healthcare, digital innovation, pharmaceuticals, medical research and technological advancement. He emphasised that India's expanding capabilities offer significant opportunities for strengthening cooperation with Sri Lanka in healthcare, education, digital transformation and economic development. Shri Nadda highlighted that India's Neighbourhood First and MAHASAGAR policies have further strengthened its enduring partnership with Sri Lanka, reflecting the shared commitment of both countries to regional stability, development and prosperity. He appreciated the important role played by the Indian diaspora in fostering mutual understanding, enhancing cultural connections and serving as a bridge between the two nations. A New Chapter in Regional Health Cooperation The First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting brought together Health Ministers and senior representatives from Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. The meeting was chaired by Sri Lanka's Minister of Health and Mass Media, Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa. The unanimously adopted Joint Ministerial Statement reaffirmed the decision to convene BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meetings and Senior Officials’ Meetings every two years, ensuring sustained engagement and follow-up on agreed regional priorities. Thailand's offer to host the Second BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting in 2028 was also welcomed. Concluding his address, Shri Nadda expressed appreciation to the Government of Sri Lanka for hosting the historic meeting and reaffirmed India's commitment to building a healthier, safer and more resilient BIMSTEC region. He emphasised that “No country should be left behind in its pursuit of better health outcomes.” The unanimous adoption of the Joint Ministerial Statement, the advancement of a common regional public health roadmap, India's commitment to hosting the Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine, and the significant bilateral healthcare initiatives with Sri Lanka and Nepal mark an important step towards strengthening regional health security and deepening India's healthcare partnerships. Together, these engagements reinforce India's commitment to translating regional cooperation into meaningful outcomes for people, guided by the vision of inclusive development, shared prosperity and “One Earth, One Family, One Future.” ***** SR HFW/Union Health Minister Addresses 1 st BIMSTEC Health Minister’s Meeting/11 November 2026/2
